D1 research authoring, batch 81 (2026-09-27): two ASSOCIATION_ONLY draft mappings added at ranks 1 and 2 (chronic-sinusitis, asthma) pending qualified-human citation verification under docs/citation-verification-sop.md; mapping approval is not citation verification. This is the first batch in which any queued file's two edges are both definitional rather than causal, and the distinction is recorded on the face of both edges rather than left implicit.

Classification and definitional guard: BOTH edges assert association only (etiologicalConsensus NOT_ESTABLISHED, vaNexusProbabilityAlignment NOT_ASSERTED, hypothesizedOnly:true) at SYSTEMIC_INFLAMMATORY, and BOTH causation statuses state explicitly that chronic rhinosinusitis with nasal polyposis and asthma are criteria that DEFINE Samter's triad, so that asserting the syndrome causes either component is circular. The edges are registered as co-occurrences requiring INDEPENDENT clinical documentation, not as consequences of the syndrome. The operational point is recorded in both rationales: a veteran whose record carries only the composite label Samter's triad has not thereby had either component characterised by extent, side, severity, or treatment, and the located evidence describes the sinus disease as aggressive, recurrent, and frequently requiring repeat endoscopic sinus surgery, so the omission has clinical and not merely administrative consequences. Both edges require separate signed otolaryngology and pulmonology documentation, objective testing, and aspirin-challenge status before the component can be treated as established.

Withheld routes and duplicate-scope screen: no nasal-polyps edge (DUPLICATE-SCOPE - the registry already carries a direct nasal-polyps to asthma edge, and because this file's rank 2 asthma edge is authored in the same batch, a syndrome-to-polyp edge would register the same asthma-polyposity relationship a second time at a different level of indirection and add a direct-versus-chain redundancy conflict to the standing CRG review set; the nasal-polyps identity therefore remains at zero registered incoming edges, which is recorded here as a deliberate and reversible choice rather than an oversight); no allergic-rhinitis edge (SCOPE - outside the three defining criteria and not supported by the located anchors, which describe the upper-airway component as chronic rhinosinusitis with polyposis rather than as allergic rhinitis); and no aspirin-intolerance or drug-hypersensitivity edge, which would be a MISSING IDENTITY since the catalog carries no NSAID-exacerbated respiratory disease or aspirin hypersensitivity identity. That last is recorded as a catalog gap worth a future expansion wave, since the drug-intolerance criterion is the component that distinguishes this syndrome from ordinary asthma with chronic rhinosinusitis.

nexusClaim.associationBasis: The one edge in this file that can be stated without qualification is chronic rhinosinusitis, because it is a definitional component of the syndrome rather than a consequence inferred from it, and the located evidence describes the phenotype precisely enough to make the co-occurrence specific: a 2024 mechanistic and management review of nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drug-exacerbated respiratory disease characterises the syndrome by the simultaneous presence of asthma, chronic rhinosinusitis with nasal polyposis, and nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drug and aspirin intolerance, and states that despite maximal and comprehensive medical treatment the disease tends to be severe, with difficult-to-treat asthma and highly aggressive and recurrent ethmoidal polyposis (PMID 39665076); a 2023 unified-airway review of aspirin-exacerbated respiratory disease characterises the condition by abnormal arachidonic acid metabolism leading to chronic rhinosinusitis with nasal polyposis, asthma, and upper and lower respiratory symptoms following ingestion of cyclooxygenase-1-inhibiting nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs, and reports that conventional medical management for both asthma and chronic rhinosinusitis with nasal polyposis is often inadequate, with endoscopic sinus surgery followed by continued medical management and optional aspirin desensitization frequently improving symptoms and objective disease measures (PMID 36283868); and the 2025 Clinical Practice Guideline on Adult Sinusitis supplies the current diagnostic and management standard against which the syndrome's sinus component is evaluated (PMID 40741969); recorded as documented co-occurrence requiring separate documentation, expressly NOT as a claim that the syndrome causes its own defining component.
nexusClaim.causationStatus: No causal claim is made or available here, and the edge's own causation status says so directly: chronic rhinosinusitis with nasal polyposis is one of the three criteria that define this syndrome, so an assertion that the syndrome produces the sinusitis is circular and is expressly disclaimed rather than argued. What the edge records is a co-occurrence with a distinct operational consequence, namely that a veteran whose record carries only the label Samter's triad has not thereby had chronic rhinosinusitis independently documented, characterised by extent, side, and severity, or linked to a treatment plan, and the located evidence shows this matters because the sinus disease is described as highly aggressive, recurrent, and frequently requiring repeat endoscopic sinus surgery. The treatment gradient is also carried openly: the located reviews attribute symptom improvement to surgery plus desensitization, which means the functional burden attributed to the syndrome is partly treatment-dependent and cannot be assigned to disease alone. Individual claims require a dated otolaryngology assessment with endoscopy or imaging documenting chronic rhinosinusitis independently of the triad label, documented extent and polyp burden, and a treatment timeline.

causalMechanism.primaryVector: The hypothesised vector is a shared type-2 inflammatory circuit with abnormal arachidonic acid metabolism producing the characteristic upper and lower airway phenotype, in which the same inflammatory process is expressed as nasal polyposis and chronic rhinosinusitis in the upper airway and as asthma in the lower airway, and in which cyclooxygenase-1 inhibition by aspirin or other nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs shunts arachidonic acid toward cysteinyl leukotrienes, amplifying the same inflammation; the circuit is named as unified precisely because the located evidence describes the upper and lower airway manifestations as one process rather than as sequential spread, and the resulting clinical pattern is a single inflammatory disease presenting in two anatomical compartments rather than one condition causing another.

evidentiaryProfile.conservativeRationale: Authored at ASSOCIATION_ONLY at mechanistic-review, unified-airway-review, and clinical-practice-guideline class, and at a deliberately different strength from a causal edge: both edges in this file are definitional co-occurrences rather than causal progressions, and the conservative standard therefore frames them as co-occurrences requiring INDEPENDENT clinical documentation rather than as consequences of the syndrome, with each target's own separate documentation, treatment, and objective testing required before the condition can be treated as established. The mechanistic review supplies the composite phenotype definition and the severe, recurrent, aggressive-polyposis characterisation (PMID 39665076); the unified-airway review supplies the arachidonic-acid mechanism, the drug-trigger relation, and the explicit statement that conventional management of both the asthma and the chronic rhinosinusitis components is often inadequate (PMID 36283868); and the adult sinusitis clinical practice guideline supplies the current diagnostic and management standard against which the sinus component must be evaluated (PMID 40741969). Because the relationship is definitional rather than causal, the conservative standard holds both edges at ASSOCIATION_ONLY with etiologicalConsensus NOT_ESTABLISHED and requires separate signed documentation for each component rather than permitting the composite label to substitute for it.
evidentiaryProfile.evidenceGaps: All three anchors describe the syndrome rather than testing an exposure-outcome relationship, so none of them is evidence of causation and none should be cited as such; the two review articles are narrative syntheses without systematic search, without quality appraisal reported in the abstract, and without pooled estimates; the characterisation of highly aggressive recurrent ethmoidal polyposis and of difficult-to-treat asthma is qualitative and unreferenced in the located abstracts, so its magnitude cannot be quantified from these sources; the clinical practice guideline covers adult sinusitis generally rather than the aspirin-exacerbated subtype, so it supplies the standard of evaluation rather than syndrome-specific evidence; and the located abstracts report no prevalence of chronic rhinosinusitis within diagnosed syndrome cohorts, because by definition all of them have it, which is the clearest demonstration that this edge carries no epidemiological information beyond the definition. Nasal-polyps was reviewed and withheld as DUPLICATE-SCOPE because the registry already carries a direct nasal-polyps to asthma edge, and authoring a syndrome-to-polyp edge alongside this file's asthma edge would register the same asthma-polyposity relationship twice at different indirection levels and add a direct-versus-chain redundancy conflict to the standing CRG review set.
alternativeEtiologiesToRuleOut: Chronic rhinosinusitis or nasal polyposis arising independently of this syndrome, including allergic fungal rhinosinusitis and antrochoanal polyp disease
Aspirin or nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drug intolerance arising outside the respiratory phenotype, such as in chronic spontaneous urticaria or cross-reactive food intolerance
Severe chronic rhinosinusitis after prior endoscopic sinus surgery, where recurrence may reflect surgical technique rather than the syndrome
An alternative unified-airway diagnosis such as eosinophilic granulomatosis with polyangiitis, allergic bronchopulmonary aspergillosis, or cystic fibrosis

suggestions.rationale: Authoring registers this edge because chronic rhinosinusitis is a definitional component of the syndrome and a veteran carrying only the composite label has not had that component independently documented, which is an operationally real gap in a benefits record, and because the located evidence characterises the sinus disease as aggressive, recurrent, and frequently requiring repeat surgery, which establishes that the omission has clinical rather than merely administrative consequences. The conservative framing states the circularity of any causal reading explicitly in the causation status rather than arguing around it, and requires independent otolaryngology documentation with endoscopy or imaging before the condition can be treated as established.

nexusClaim.associationBasis: Asthma is the second definitional component of this syndrome, and the located evidence describes its severity and the consequences of treating it jointly with the sinus component: the 2024 mechanistic and management review characterises the syndrome as the simultaneous presence of asthma, chronic rhinosinusitis with nasal polyposis, and nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drug and aspirin intolerance, and states that despite maximal and comprehensive medical treatment the disease tends to be severe, with difficult-to-treat asthma specifically named as a feature (PMID 39665076); the 2023 unified-airway review states that diagnosis is clinical and may involve an aspirin challenge, that inflammatory biomarkers may be useful for diagnosis and treatment monitoring, and that conventional medical management for asthma and chronic rhinosinusitis with nasal polyposis is often inadequate, with endoscopic sinus surgery followed by continued medical management and or without aspirin desensitization frequently improving symptoms and objective disease measures (PMID 36283868); and a 2026 surgical-outcome cohort of 70 patients with chronic rhinosinusitis with nasal polyps and comorbid asthma undergoing revision endoscopic sinus surgery provides quantified evidence that the asthma and sinus disease behave as one treatment unit, showing that patients with a preoperative Completeness of Surgery Index below 70 had significantly greater improvement on both the sino-nasal outcome test and the Asthma Control Test, with the asthma-control improvement reaching 3.9 versus 0.88 in uncontrolled asthma (p=0.029) (PMID 41045292); recorded as documented co-occurrence requiring separate documentation, expressly NOT as a claim that the syndrome causes its own defining component.
nexusClaim.causationStatus: No causal claim is made or available here, and the causation status disclaims the circular reading explicitly: asthma is one of the three criteria defining this syndrome, so asserting that the syndrome produces the asthma is circular. The located surgery cohort is the only anchor that reports a quantitative asthma outcome, and it is registered as evidence that the two components respond to a shared intervention rather than as evidence of causation between them, because what it demonstrates is that incomplete sinus surgery predicts worse asthma control after revision, which is a statement about coupled treatment response and not about one condition producing the other. The severity characterisation in the review anchors is qualitative and unreferenced in the located abstracts, so its magnitude cannot be quantified from these sources, and no located anchor reports a prevalence of severe or difficult-to-treat asthma within diagnosed syndrome cohorts, because by definition all of them have asthma. Individual claims require a dated pulmonology assessment documenting asthma severity, control, and current therapy independently of the triad label, plus documentation of whether an aspirin challenge was performed and with what result.

causalMechanism.primaryVector: The hypothesised vector is a shared type-2 inflammatory circuit with abnormal arachidonic acid metabolism, in which cyclooxygenase-1 inhibition by aspirin or other nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs shunts arachidonic acid toward cysteinyl leukotrienes that amplify eosinophilic inflammation, and in which the same process is expressed as asthma in the lower airway and as nasal polyposis in the upper airway; the vector is named as unified rather than directional because the located evidence treats the upper and lower airway manifestations as one process, and the surgery cohort is offered as the strongest located support, since it shows asthma control improving in step with sinus surgical completeness.

evidentiaryProfile.conservativeRationale: Authored at ASSOCIATION_ONLY at mechanistic-review, unified-airway-review, and surgical-outcome-cohort class, deliberately parallel to the file's rank 1 chronic-sinusitis edge and held to the same definitional standard: both components are criteria of the syndrome, and a composite label in a benefits record substitutes for neither component's independent documentation. The mechanistic review supplies the composite definition and the difficult-to-treat asthma characterisation (PMID 39665076); the unified-airway review supplies the arachidonic-acid and leukotriene-shunt mechanism, the clinical-diagnosis and aspirin-challenge statement, and the report that conventional management of both components is often inadequate (PMID 36283868); and the surgery cohort is the only located anchor with a quantified asthma outcome, and it is registered specifically as evidence of coupled treatment response between the two airway compartments, which is the located basis for treating them as a single management unit rather than as two independent conditions (PMID 41045292). Because the relationship is definitional rather than causal, the conservative standard holds the edge at ASSOCIATION_ONLY and requires separate signed pulmonology documentation plus aspirin-challenge status.
evidentiaryProfile.evidenceGaps: All three anchors are reviews or a surgical cohort and none tests an exposure-outcome relationship, so none is evidence of causation; the mechanistic and unified-airway reviews are narrative syntheses without reported systematic search, quality appraisal, or pooled estimates; the surgical cohort of 70 patients is single-institution, consists entirely of patients already selected for revision surgery after prior incomplete surgery, and therefore contains no treatment-naive comparator, so its 3.9-versus-0.88 Asthma Control Test improvement is a within-group before-and-after contrast in a selected population; the cohort's asthma subgroup with uncontrolled asthma is not reported as a count in the located abstract, so the 3.9-versus-0.88 comparison rests on an unstated denominator; the Completeness of Surgery Index is a radiologic scoring system and its threshold of 70 is not independently validated in the located abstract; no located anchor reports severe-asthma prevalence in diagnosed syndrome cohorts, because by definition all patients have asthma; and no located anchor reports outcomes stratified by whether aspirin desensitization was performed. Allergic-rhinitis and eustachian-tube or hearing outcomes were reviewed and not authored, as were both outside the three defining criteria and unsupported by the located anchors.
alternativeEtiologiesToRuleOut: Severe or difficult-to-treat asthma arising independently of this syndrome, including eosinophilic granulomatosis with polyangiitis and allergic bronchopulmonary aspergillosis
Asthma exacerbation driven by a respiratory infection or by non-adherence rather than by the syndrome's inflammatory circuit
Bronchial asthma induced or worsened by nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drug exposure, which is a drug effect rather than a disease consequence
An occupational or irritant-induced asthma phenotype coexisting with the syndrome

evidenceGaps: All three anchors are reviews or a surgical cohort and none tests an exposure-outcome relationship, so none is evidence of causation; the mechanistic and unified-airway reviews are narrative syntheses without reported systematic search, quality appraisal, or pooled estimates; the surgical cohort of 70 patients is single-institution, consists entirely of patients already selected for revision surgery after prior incomplete surgery, and therefore contains no treatment-naive comparator, so its 3.9-versus-0.88 Asthma Control Test improvement is a within-group before-and-after contrast in a selected population; the cohort's asthma subgroup with uncontrolled asthma is not reported as a count in the located abstract, so the 3.9-versus-0.88 comparison rests on an unstated denominator; the Completeness of Surgery Index is a radiologic scoring system and its threshold of 70 is not independently validated in the located abstract; no located anchor reports severe-asthma prevalence in diagnosed syndrome cohorts, because by definition all patients have asthma; and no located anchor reports outcomes stratified by whether aspirin desensitization was performed. Allergic-rhinitis and eustachian-tube or hearing outcomes were reviewed and not authored, as were both outside the three defining criteria and unsupported by the located anchors.
suggestions.rationale: Authoring registers this edge because asthma is a definitional component of the syndrome, because the located evidence names difficult-to-treat asthma as a characteristic feature, and because the surgical cohort supplies the only located demonstration that the sinus and asthma components respond as one coupled treatment unit, which is directly relevant to how a benefits examiner should treat a single composite diagnosis. The conservative framing disclaims the circular causal reading in the causation status, registers the surgery cohort as coupled-treatment-response evidence rather than causal evidence, notes the unstated asthma-subgroup denominator, and requires independent pulmonology documentation with aspirin-challenge status.
